sources.title: Berdysycran-depe and the chronology of the Oxus Civilization
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronology and distribution study defining Middle and Late Bronze Age BMAC phases.

sources.title: Lyonnet and Dubova, Questioning the Oxus Civilization or BMAC
sources.note: Scholarly overview of regional chronology, settlements, subsistence, institutions, writing, and contested interpretations.

sources.title: Climate Change and the Rise and Fall of the Oxus Civilization
sources.note: Scholarly reassessment of water, settlement movement, chronology, and environmental explanations for change.

sources.title: UNESCO Ancient Merv World Heritage nomination
sources.note: Official nomination documenting Bronze Age Margiana centers, settlement plans, storage, rebuilding, and later villages.

sources.title: Kaniuth, The Bronze Age Settlement of the Pashkhurt Valley
sources.note: University-hosted excavation synthesis on rural settlement, farming, herding, irrigation, and regional connections.

sources.title: Agriculture and herding in early Oxus oasis settlements
sources.note: Antiquity study of crops, animals, and mixed oasis economies in early Oxus settlements.

sources.title: Seeds of Time: archaeobotany in southern Central Asia
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed archaeobotanical study distinguishing crops, legumes, fruits, and managed wild resources.

sources.title: Rise of bronze in Central Asia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed compositional and provenance analysis of Central Asian copper, tin bronze, ores, and exchange.

sources.title: Manufacturing and trade of Asian elephant ivory at Gonur Depe
sources.note: Peer-reviewed technological study of imported raw material, local manufacture, artifacts, and social contexts.

sources.title: Metalworkers workshops at Gonur and other BMAC sites
sources.note: Open scholarly proceedings chapter documenting industrial rooms, kilns, molds, crucibles, and regional metalworking.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum, Art of the Bronze Age
sources.note: Museum catalogue placing vessels, ornaments, seals, and materials within wider Bronze Age connections.

sources.title: British Museum BMAC compartmented stamp seal
sources.note: Museum object record for a copper-alloy stamp seal, its motifs, associations, and uncertain find context.

sources.title: British Museum BMAC ram-shaped cosmetic bottle
sources.note: Museum object record explaining material, probable function, comparative culture, and acquisition history.

sources.title: New polychrome painting from Gonur Depe
sources.note: Antiquity report on a rare painted object, its grave context, materials, technology, and interpretive limits.

sources.title: Kufterin and Dubova, skeletal remains from Gonur Depe
sources.note: Bioarchaeological study of mortality, childhood stress, teeth, joints, trauma, and sample limitations.

sources.title: Formation of human populations in South and Central Asia, supplement
sources.note: Official Science ancient-DNA supplement on Gonur individuals, ancestry variation, mobility, and wider interaction.

sources.title: Funerary rituals and archaeothanatology in BMAC graves
sources.note: Scholarly chapter applying archaeothanatology to grave construction, body placement, reopening, and regional difference.

sources.title: The Necropolis of Gonur
sources.note: Excavation volume documenting grave types, age distributions, objects, animal deposits, and preservation.

sources.title: CNR repository, Adji Kui graveyard in Margiana
sources.note: Italian National Research Council record for excavation of a Bronze Age graveyard and settlement context.

sources.title: Society for the Exploration of EurAsia, Gonur magnetometry
sources.note: Research-project report mapping residential sectors, workshops, ovens, graves, and subsurface anomalies at Gonur.

sources.title: Margiana exhibition wall texts, Museum of Prehistory and Early History
sources.note: Museum exhibition text on Gonur planning, houses, crafts, seals, graves, and the limits of surviving writing.

sources.title: Silent partners: mobility and interaction in Central Asia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of Oxus interaction, mobility, complex organization, and nomadic-sedentary relationships.

sources.title: Production evidence for the origins of the Oxus Civilization
sources.note: Antiquity study using production evidence to examine origins and regional development without assuming invasion.

sources.title: Urban Cultures of Central Asia
sources.note: Open scholarly volume on Gonur chronology, architecture, craft zones, water installations, and urban interpretation.

sources.title: Turkmenistan government report on Gonur excavations
sources.note: Official report on recent excavations, child graves, seals, ceramics, and continued archaeological work.

sources.title: Irrigating the Desert: early water management in Central Asia
sources.note: Scholarly book introduction framing evidence, terminology, chronology, and uncertainty in ancient irrigation research.
